payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Using the source-mug identity evidence, is the same mug to the right of the headphones, or is there clear evidence of movement toward that right-side relation without completion?
node.criteria: Pass only if the same source mug is reliably identified and is visibly to the right of the headphones. Fail only if the same mug is reliably identified and clear comparison shows no movement toward the right-side relation; report its source and edited positions. Unknown if identity or displacement cannot be resolved. Movement toward the right-side relation without reaching it is evidence of partial progress only when the same mug and that displacement are established; movement in another direction, a different mug on the right, or object presence alone is not progress.
node.binding: Use s1's specific identity/continuity observations, then compare the tracked mug's source and edited positions relative to the headphones. Explicitly report identity cues, displacement direction, and whether the right-side relation is achieved. Do not infer movement from the other mugs or the blue blur alone.

node_traces.evidence: The source shows one light-blue mug to the left of the headphones. The edited image shows two small mugs, one on each side of the headphones, and a blue blur on the left. Neither edited mug can be reliably matched to the source mug from the visible identity cues, so its displacement and whether it reached the right-side relation cannot be established.

The source contains one light-blue mug left of the headphones. The edited image shows two small mugs, a blue blur, and headphones; neither mug clearly matches the source mug’s distinctive light-blue color and shape, and the blur does not establish its position. The same mug’s identity and displacement therefore cannot be reliably tracked, so whether it moved toward or reached the right side is unresolved.

The source mug is the large light-blue mug with a left-side handle, positioned left of the headphones. In the edited image, that distinctive mug is not clearly identifiable: there are two smaller mugs, and a blue blur at the left, but neither establishes the same mug's identity or its displacement. Therefore the tracked mug's movement toward or achievement of the right-side relation cannot be resolved.
